questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted a host university with English as the main language.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Easy. UBC provided plenty of information on their website and as part of the exchange program.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Because of covid must information was online. We had an introduction to the university and how to thrive as a student on the canvas platform. We were also put into exchange groups on the week of arrival and got a tour guide.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: There were different housing available on campus - I ended up in Fairview Cresent where most exchange student get a spot. However due to covid the spots were limited.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: You can buy a meal plan if you'd like. However it is mostly first year students who do this. All housing on campus has a shared kitchen in the unit you stay in.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: The housing on campus are in pretty bad conditions and the sound isolation is really bad. I you are sensitive to noise and you do not like to stay up late, I would not recommend campus housing. Then again it really depends on which roomies you end up with. On campus is also pretty isolated and you get pretty bored with looking at the same buildings every day. I would recommend to find something off campus to experience more of the Canadian lifestyle.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was pretty messy because of covid - I was suppose to go on exchange in 2020 but ended up going in 2021, so I had to register for courses twice, but this is of course not UBC's fault. However - you need to make a priority list of 10 courses, which can be quite hard.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I didn't really use the help provided, so I am not sure..

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all my first priorities.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be sure to see if the courses you want to sign up for are running during the term you are on exchange - most of them only run during the fall or spring.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took 300-level classes because I was in my 3rd year. But it is possible to take all kind of levels.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The style of teachings were very different in each of my course. The biggest difference is that in the Canadian school system they divide their exams into many pieces, which meant that I had two midterms during my term and one final exam in each course. This made me more stressed in the beginning but during my finals I has more time.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
PHIL 332A Environmental Ethics
SOCI 301 Sociology of Development
SOCI 310 Canadian Society

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I really loved Environmental Ethics! It was challenging since I am used to studying anthropology but it was really interesting to learn how to argue in philosophy. The course very strait forward in it structure which made it easy to know what to suspect. And the topics were just very interesting - everything from First Nation perspectives on the environments to ecofeminism and climate change. The main goal was to discuss the moral problems arising in the context of human relationships to  nature and to non-human living things.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I went on quite a few trips, when we had to rent cars, pay for gas etc. I also did a lot of skiing where I had to rent skies, boots etc.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Groceries on campus was really expensive, but I you take a bus foe 15 minutes to the nearest No Frills you can save a looot of money.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There is about 300 clubs that you can sign up for. There is also a recreation center with a gym, swimming facilities, dance classes, yoga classes, and martial arts - there is a free week to try out the classes and then you can sign up for a semester or 2.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Go skiing in Whistler!! Buy a season pass (for students) and ski from november-april! You can rent skies and boots in Sports Junkies in Vancouver.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
During the summer: There are plenty of hikes to do in the area. Sign up for evo cars and rent them easily. Go to Vancouver Island and Tofino to surf. 
During winter: Whistler for skiing. In Vancouver there's plenty of cinemas and restaurants to explore.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Sign up for some of the clubs or try to find some study partners in your classes.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: To say "How are you" all the time:)

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The friendly and kindness of Canadians!

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Prepare what you want to see before you go to Canada! Otherwise you'll stress about it the first week which is a waste of time! 
2. Get a approval of your drivers license from your home country (traffikstyrelsen) so that you can rent evo cars. 
3. Spent as much time in nature as possible!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Figure out what your priorities should be and what you want to spent most time on: school, making new connections, exploring nature, skiing, volunteering, working etc.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The academically part was definitely most rewarding: learning to navigate in another educational system, being challenged on my academical knowledge, and forced out of my comfort zone.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Being away from my home and friends for that long was quite challenging.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
